title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1965 'Théorie de Galois des motifs' notes, Grothendieck studies A-linear categories C (for him, categories of motives or lattices with multiplications) that are Morita-equivalent to P(σ), the category of finitely generated projective modules over an order σ. The previous page attaches to such a C its Gr-category End(C) of autoequivalences, whose invariants are the Brandt (Picard-type) group of invertible bimodules, the units of the centre, and a class in H^3.

Step 1. Grothendieck considers two 2-groupoids:
- Brd: objects are rings σ (orders) in a given class; 1-morphisms are invertible bimodules (bitorsors); 2-morphisms are bimodule isomorphisms; composition is ⊗.
- D: the 2-groupoid of the corresponding 'Deligne' categories.
The 2-functor σ ↦ C_σ = P(σ) is a 2-equivalence. This is Morita theory. He notes there is no natural 2-functor in the reverse direction: recovering a ring from C requires choosing a generator X and taking σ = End_C(X). A pseudo-inverse exists only after such a choice.

Step 2. From now on he restricts to the case where the σ are Azumaya algebras over A. Intrinsically, the centre of C is A, i.e. A ≅ End(id_C).

Step 3. He attaches to C, without choosing a ring, a G_m-gerbe over Spec A. For an A-scheme T, Ban(C)(T) is the category of A-linear functors φ: C → Mod(O_T) such that, for X in C (one X or all X, 'c'est pareil') with σ = End_C(X), the σ⊗_A O_T-module φ(X) is a banalisation (splitting) of σ. That is, φ(X) = E is locally free and σ⊗O_T ≅ End_{O_T}(E). An earlier, wrong condition 'localement libre de rang 1' is crossed out and replaced by this.

Step 4. Claim: evaluation φ ↦ φ(X) is an equivalence between the fibred category T ↦ Ban(C)(T) and the fibred category of banalisations of σ. The latter is the gerbe of trivialisations of the Azumaya algebra σ:
- it is locally non-empty, since σ splits étale or fppf locally;
- any two splittings are locally isomorphic;
- automorphisms of a splitting are G_m.
So Ban(C) is a gerbe with band G_m, whose class in H^2(A, G_m) is the Brauer class of σ. The resulting gerbe is independent of X up to canonical equivalence, because changing X changes σ by an invertible bimodule.

Purpose (made explicit on the next page): 
- C embeds fully faithfully into Rep(G) as the weight-1 locally free representations of locally constant rank n(x).
- Hence a 'Dedekind–Azumaya category' is the same as a G_m-gerbe plus a rank function, such that the gerbe is locally given by an Azumaya algebra of that rank.
- This lets him define det X as a weight-n representation of the gerbe, compatible with the reduced norm.
The whole construction is a ring-free, intrinsic (Tannakian-flavoured, but non-tensor) description of the Brauer class of the endomorphism algebras of motives.
errors: No real mathematical error on this page. The crossed-out first condition, that φ(X) be 'localement libre de rang 1', would be wrong over σ; Grothendieck himself corrects it to 'banalisation de σ'.

Minor gap: identifying A-linear functors C → Mod(O_T) with σ⊗O_T-modules via φ ↦ φ(X) implicitly uses C ≃ P(σ) (idempotent-complete, generated by X). The variance (left σ-module vs σ^op) is not discussed.
'Ban_T(C)(T)' in the last paragraph is a slip for Ban(C)(T).

ideas.what: 2-equivalence between the 2-groupoid of rings/orders with invertible bimodules (Brandt groupoids) and the 2-groupoid of linear categories P(σ), with no canonical inverse because a generator must be chosen
ideas.usually_credited_to: Morita (1958), Bass (Algebraic K-theory, 1968); bicategorical formulation by Bénabou and later authors

ideas.what: Gerbe of banalisations (splittings) of an Azumaya algebra, with band G_m, whose class is the Brauer class
ideas.modern_name: Gerbe of trivialisations of an Azumaya algebra; Brauer class as a G_m-gerbe
ideas.usually_credited_to: Giraud (Cohomologie non abélienne, 1966 thesis / 1971 book); Grothendieck, Le groupe de Brauer I (1966)
ideas.where_published: Possibly Le groupe de Brauer I–III (Dix exposés); unsure of the exact formulation there

ideas.what: Intrinsic definition of the gerbe directly from the A-linear category C, as A-linear 'fibre functors' C → Mod(O_T) splitting End(X), independent of the generator X
ideas.modern_name: Gerbe of fibre functors of a twisted form of Vect / Morita-invariant Brauer class of a linear category (non-tensor analogue of the Tannakian gerbe of fibre functors)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Saavedra Rivano (1972) and Deligne (1990) in the tensor setting; Lieblich, Antieau–Gepner and Toën for linear/derived categories

ideas.what: (Completed on the next page) C ≃ weight-1 locally free representations of the gerbe of given rank; Azumaya category = G_m-gerbe + rank function
ideas.modern_name: Modules over an Azumaya algebra ≃ twisted sheaves (Căldăraru, Lieblich)

missed.claim: In 1965 Grothendieck defines the G_m-gerbe attached to an Azumaya-type linear category intrinsically, as the stack of A-linear functors C → Mod(O_T) that split End(X). This is a non-tensor 'fibre functor' construction anticipating both Saavedra's Tannakian gerbes and the twisted-sheaf description of modules over Azumaya algebras. It was used here to attach Brauer classes and determinants (via the reduced norm) to motives with multiplication.
missed.quote: on définit la catégorie des banalisations de C sur T ... comme la catégorie des foncteurs A-linéaires φ : C → Mod(O_T) ... c'est donc une gerbe de liens G_m. D'ailleurs l'équivalence de ces gerbes ne dépend pas du choix de X.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an early, generator-free (Morita-invariant) formulation of the Brauer class of a linear category. The theory of twisted sheaves and Brauer classes of categories (Lieblich, Antieau–Gepner, Toën) credits later authors. Its motivic use — Brauer classes and determinants of motives with endomorphism algebras — is a thread that is little developed in this form.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is correct and fairly standard by today's standards (Giraud gerbes, twisted sheaves). Its interest lies in the date (1965, before Giraud's book and Saavedra), the intrinsic fibre-functor style definition from the linear category alone, and the motivic setting. This is a notable early unpublished formulation, but not a result unknown to specialists.
transcription_corrections: 'On s'intéresse par la suite qu'aux' should read 'On ne s'intéresse par la suite qu'aux'; from context the topic is the categories C whose σ are Azumaya algebras.
'A ⥲ End(L_C)' is most likely 'A ⥲ End(id_C)' (or End(1_C)), i.e. the centre of C is A.
'pour [-A-] schéma T sur A' likely reads 'pour tout schéma T sur A'.
'Ban_T(C)(T)' should be 'Ban(C)(T)' (the fibred category T ↦ Ban(C)(T)).

In the defining condition: 'Pour un X ∈ C (ou tout X ∈ Ob C, c'est pareil) posons σ = End_C(X), φ(X) considéré comme σ⊗_A O_T-Module est une banalisation de σ'; the crossed-out text read 'localement libre de rang 1'.
The crossed-out line 'Rep_T(C) ... est un champ pour la top. fppf' is correctly identified as deleted.
